idiom_name: explicit return types; void marks 'result not meant to be used'
implementation_notes: TypeScript states the contract in the signature: annotate the return type and the caller can see whether a function produces a value (T, Promise<T>, a readonly array) or is a procedure whose result is not meant to be used (void). void is exactly that marker - a contextual function type returning void accepts an implementation that returns a value and discards it, which is what makes arr.forEach((el) => out.push(el)) type-check even though push returns a number. The type system therefore documents the interesting return value but cannot require its use, so pair explicit return types with lint rules (the no-unused-expressions and array-callback-return family) where a dropped result is a defect.
pitfalls: void in a function type does not stop an implementation from returning a value - it is discarded - so a typed callback can drop a result the caller expected to be used.
Without an explicit return type the compiler infers a union of every returned expression, so a forgotten return widens the type to include undefined and only fails later at the call site.
any and as at untyped boundaries (JSON.parse, untyped libraries) reintroduce values with no declared return contract, so the discipline has to be re-established in the wrapper.
